title: Saint Eusebius of Vercelli, Bishop
short_summary: Saint Eusebius of Vercelli was a fourth-century bishop who joined a common life of prayer with his clergy and endured exile for defending the Nicene faith against Arianism.
key_facts: The Church permits his optional memorial on August 3.
He became bishop of Vercelli in northern Italy around the year 340.
He is remembered for uniting his clergy in a common life of prayer while serving the diocese.
Emperor Constantius II exiled him for refusing to condemn Saint Athanasius.

sections.heading: A bishop who lived among his clergy
sections.body: Eusebius is remembered as one of the first Western bishops to gather his clergy into a common household of prayer and shared life while they continued their pastoral duties, joining the discipline of monastic life to the ordinary work of a diocese.

sections.heading: Defender of the Nicene faith
sections.body: At a council convened in Milan in 355, Eusebius refused pressure from Emperor Constantius II to condemn Saint Athanasius and sign an Arian formula. His steadfastness cost him exile to the eastern provinces of the empire for several years.

sections.heading: Exile and return
sections.body: During his exile Eusebius endured harsh treatment in different eastern locations before he was allowed to return to Vercelli after the accession of Emperor Julian. He continued to govern his diocese until his death.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Fidelity under pressure
catholic_connection_sections.body: Eusebius's refusal to bend to imperial pressure over the Nicene faith is a witness that the truth about Christ cannot be settled by political power.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Common life and pastoral care
catholic_connection_sections.body: His practice of gathering clergy into shared prayer and life points to the ancient link between personal holiness and pastoral service.
